sections.title: Diagnosis Summary
sections.content:
**Primary Risk: Communication & Confidence Risk (ownership + behavioural signal under pressure).**

Shubham, your profile reads credibly for **operations and quality in manufacturing**: shop-floor leadership (14-person team), measurable line and adherence gains, **NCR/corrective-action** discipline, **5S/Kaizen**, heavy **documentation & audit** rigor (130+ quality documents, **98% audit compliance**), cross-functional coordination, plus **SAP MM** and Coursera supply-chain grounding. **Technical Readiness (2.2)** sits slightly below your other mid-band scores—often where **method vocabulary** (SPC, CAPA, 8D, control plans) meets **live explanation** under follow-up.

The standout gap is **Behavioural Story (1.75)**—your lowest dimension. In interviews this typically shows up as **undersold ownership**: you *did* the work (KPI huddles, NCR closures, project reviews) but may **sound like a participant** instead of the person who **prioritized, decided, and drove** the outcome. **Communication & Confidence Risk** means interviewers may **under-weight** your resume because delivery feels **hesitant, generic, or metric-light** when probed.

**Mapping Rule Insight:**
- Your **Resume & Experience Clarity (2.4)** and **Role-Specific Technical (2.4)** give enough raw material for screening.
- To convert, answers must **pair every KPI with a decision you owned** and **one conflict or trade-off** (capacity vs quality, speed vs documentation, client vs internal standard).
- Confidence here is **trained**: louder isn’t the fix—**crisper structure + proof** is.

sections.title: How This Risk Shows Up in Interviews
sections.content:
**Scenario A: The "Tell me about yourself" / Ops arc**

**Red Flag Prompt:** "Walk me through your time at Track Components—what were you accountable for on the floor versus what the line leads owned?"

**Likely Breakdown:** You may describe **activities** (huddles, reviews, documents) without a **clear accountability line**: what **only you** could escalate, approve, or stop the line for—and **what metric moved** because of it.

---

**Scenario B: Quality system depth**

**Red Flag Prompt:** "You closed 3–4 NCRs monthly and cut repeat non-conformance by 12% in six weeks—**how** did you know repeat issues were the same root cause, and what changed in the work instruction?"

**Likely Breakdown:** With **Technical Readiness 2.2**, you might stay at **story level** and struggle to **sequence** root-cause method, verification, and **sustainment** (training, audit spot-checks). That reads as **buzzwords** without **system thinking**.

---

**Scenario C: Stakeholder / pressure**

**Red Flag Prompt:** "Give me a time production and quality disagreed on releasing a batch. What did you push for, and what was the result?"

**Likely Breakdown:** **Behavioural Story 1.75** shows up as **missing tension**: no named stakeholder, no trade-off, no **before/after**. Without conflict, you sound **nice** but not **influential**.

sections.title: Priority Fix Order

steps.title: Ownership Language + STAR for Top 5 Bullets
steps.content: Rewrite Track Components + Unitech highlights as **60-second STAR**: **I owned / I decided / I escalated** (one per story) + **one number**. Drop filler adjectives. **Score Target:** Behavioural Story 1.75 → 3.5

steps.title: Quality & Ops Technical Defense (NCR, 5S, KPI, SAP MM)
steps.content: Prepare crisp definitions you can say in **20 seconds**: NCR vs CAPA, how you **verify** corrective action, how **5S/Kaizen** tied to the **7% adherence** or **20% line** improvement, and **SAP MM** PR-PO-GR-IR in your own project words. **Score Target:** Technical Readiness 2.2 → 3.8, Role-Specific Technical 2.4 → 4.0

steps.title: Answer Structure Under Interruption
steps.content: Practice **Problem → What I owned → Steps → Metric → Risk if we didn’t act** in **45 seconds**. Mentor interrupts mid-answer; you **finish the metric** before elaborating. **Score Target:** Answer Structure 2.4 → 4.0

steps.title: Pressure Mocks (Ops + Quality + Graduate story)
steps.content: Full simulation: Galway master’s tie-in to **why ops in Ireland**, Unitech planning discipline, Magson internship ownership. **Score Target:** Overall band ≥ 4.0, Resume clarity 2.4 → 4.2

sections.content: Sequence matters: **behavioural ownership first**—without it, technical depth won’t register as leadership potential.

sections.title: Resume-Anchored Technical Prep
sections.content:
**Highlight 1: Track Components — 14-person shop-floor quality, ~20% line performance, KPI huddles, ~7% adherence**

- **Interviewer Probe:** "Which KPIs were on the huddle board, and what **one** downtime action did you prioritize when two lines competed for the same maintenance window?"
- **Prep Drill:** Name **3 KPIs** + **one real trade-off** you navigated.

---

**Highlight 2: NCRs 3–4/month, repeat non-conformance −12% in 6 weeks, work instructions**

- **Interviewer Probe:** "Walk me from **detection** to **closure**—who signs off, what proves effectiveness?"
- **Prep Drill:** **One** NCR storyline: symptom → root cause tool (5 Why / fishbone—pick what you used) → corrective action → how you **proved** repeat issues stopped.

---

**Highlight 3: 130+ quality documents, 98% audit compliance**

- **Interviewer Probe:** "What failed most often in audits before, and what **process** changed in how you authored or controlled documents?"
- **Prep Drill:** Link **document control** to **traceability** and **one audit finding** you eliminated.

---

**Highlight 4: Unitech — planning, on-time delivery +8%, Tally dashboard, −10 hrs/week manual reporting**

- **Interviewer Probe:** "What did the dashboard change in **decisions**, not just reporting?"
- **Prep Drill:** **Before/after** decision example in **one sentence**.

---

**Highlight 5: SAP MM project — PR-PO-GR-IR, inventory**

- **Interviewer Probe:** "Where could stock or procurement go wrong in your design, and how did you **reconcile** GR-IR?"
- **Prep Drill:** **Happy path + one exception path** (e.g. partial delivery, price mismatch) in plain language.

sections.title: Interview Answer Construction Guidance
sections.content:
**Prompt:** "Tell me about a time you improved quality or line performance at Track Components."

**Baseline Answer (Communication & Confidence pattern):**
"I worked with the team on quality and we did KPI meetings and 5S. We improved performance and reduced issues. I also worked on documents for audits."

**Fixed Answer (4.0+ quality):**
"We had recurring line stoppages and quality noise that showed up in downtime and repeat non-conformances. (Situation) I was accountable for shop-floor quality with a 14-person team, so I needed to improve flow without losing audit traceability. (Task) I ran daily KPI huddles focused on top downtime drivers, aligned corrective actions with operations, and drove weekly reviews using 5S and Kaizen to tighten handoffs. (Action) I also led root-cause work on NCRs—roughly 3–4 a month—updated work instructions where repeat issues appeared, and within about six weeks repeat non-conformance dropped by around 12%, while line performance improved materially alongside stronger adherence. (Result)"

**Why this works:** **Ownership verbs**, **specific mechanisms**, **numbers**, and a **clear timeline**—confidence follows structure.

sections.title: High-Risk Questions (The Landmines)
sections.content:
"How do you prioritize when **OTD** pressure conflicts with **quality hold**?" **(Risk: Behavioural Story 1.75)**

"Explain **how** you measured the 20% line improvement and ruled out normal variance." **(Risk: Technical Readiness 2.2)**

"What is your **role** versus the production manager’s in a daily KPI huddle?" **(Risk: Resume & Experience Clarity 2.4)**

"Walk me through **SAP MM** PR to IR—where do **you** intervene in a real plant?" **(Risk: Role-Specific Technical 2.4)**

"Describe a **failed** corrective action—what did you change in the approach?" **(Risk: Behavioural Story 1.75)**

"How did Galway **Master’s in International Management** change how you lead ops versus India experience?" **(Risk: Answer Structure 2.4)**

sections.title: Mock Interview Plan (Mentor-Led)

data.label: Session 1: Ownership & STAR (Track + Unitech)
data.objective: Every story ends with metric + your decision—not team effort only.

data.label: Session 2: Quality System & SAP MM
data.objective: NCR/CAPA, documentation, audit logic; SAP MM flow and exceptions.

data.label: Session 3: Conflict & Stakeholder Pressure
data.objective: Production vs quality, client vs internal standard, escalation paths.

data.label: Session 4: Full Ops/Quality Simulation
data.objective: Intro → deep resume → behavioural → technical follow-through.

sections.content:
**Session 1:** Ruthless edit of **I** vs **we**; mentor flags vague teamwork.

**Session 2:** No acronyms without **one plain-English consequence**.

**Session 3:** No story without **tension** and **resolution metric**.

**Session 4:** Mixed Ireland + India narrative coherence.

sections.title: Expected Outcome
sections.content:
**Target Average Score: 4.5** (from a ~3.14 baseline on the composite diagnostic).

**Measurable Change Expected:**
- **Ownership** is explicit in every major example; **metrics** survive "how did you measure that?"
- **Quality stories** include **method + verification**, not only outcomes.
- **Communication** reads as **calm and precise**, not loud—**confidence through preparation**.

**After Persona:** An **Operations & Quality Engineer** who sounds **accountable**, **audit-aware**, and **stakeholder-capable**—aligned with manufacturing hiring bars in Ireland and EU-quality expectations.

sections.title: How to Use This Plan

candidateSteps.title: Record three stories only (refine, don’t expand)
candidateSteps.content: Track NCR win, KPI huddle win, Unitech dashboard win—until each is under 90 seconds with metrics.

candidateSteps.title: Log confidence triggers
candidateSteps.content: Note when you rush, apologize, or trail off—fix with pause + headline metric.

candidateSteps.title: Repeat weak prompts daily
candidateSteps.content: Conflict questions and "prove the number" questions until boringly fluent.

candidateSteps.title: Gate on Behavioural Story
candidateSteps.content: Do not add new frameworks until Session 1 stories score 4.0+ on ownership.

mentorSteps.title: Demand named conflict
mentorSteps.content: If a story has no disagreement, it’s not ready—push for a real ops tension.

mentorSteps.title: Probe metrics until concrete
mentorSteps.content: Baseline, period, measurement method—no hand-waving on % improvements.

mentorSteps.title: Feedback in three bullets
mentorSteps.content: After each mock: one fix for ownership, one for evidence, one for closing impact.

mentorSteps.title: No sign-off on enthusiasm alone
mentorSteps.content: Readiness = structured answers under interruption, not positive energy.

sections.content:
**Main Rule:** Communication & confidence in hiring is mostly **clarity under stress**—train with **interruptions** and **timeboxes**.

**Suggested Timeline:**
- Week 1: Three STAR stories + ownership language
- Week 2: Sessions 1–2
- Week 3: Session 3
- Week 4: Session 4
- Week 5: Buffer if behavioural score lags

**Session Notes Placeholder:** [Insert: confidence dips, vague KPIs, SAP depth gaps, Ireland narrative.]
